name: glm-redsnow-tp2
_comment: Portable configuration example: host, user and private workspace paths are placeholders, not original measured infrastructure. Historical context follows; this is not a new qualification claim. The RED-SNOW 4.91bpw GLM-5.3-Flash pack (186 GiB: 4/5/6-bit experts mixed inside a layer, a plain-fp16 indexer wq_b) as a two-rank tensor-parallel group (lane L9, docs/GLM_TP.md section 8): N1 = rank 0, N4 = rank 1. It does not fit one node, so each rank maps the pack with its share of the routed experts (0..144 | 144..288) and reads and allocates only those: 94.6 GiB of regions a rank (the replicated trunk 8.06 GiB + its experts 86.5 GiB; no NextN layer, no vision tower). Text only: --no-vision, --prefix-cache off, --spec none --no-drafts, pinned --slots and --kv-tokens (the group plans before it loads). N2 and N3 are the gn100s: disabled by owner rule, listed so that a rank map naming them is refused.

memory._comment: a rank's regions (94.6 GiB) plus 2 slots of KDA state, the 16,384-token KV pool and the 512-row chunk's scratch, and the serving floor (8 GiB). The rank planner (tools/glm_redsnow_tp2.sh header) grants these flags from 108.4 GiB free (weights 94.61 + runtime 5.75 + floor 8.00 GiB); the box's 20 GiB headroom rule cannot hold for a 94.6 GiB rank on a 117 GiB node: about 15.5 to 16 GiB stay available while the group runs (a load drops MemAvailable 0.3 to 0.8 GiB more than its regions); the binary is this branch's, installed by tools/glm_redsnow_tp2.sh install at cluster-bin-l9 (the 2.25bpw window's cluster-bin holds a build that refuses this pack)
